To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the molecular testing of cancers for targeted therapies is medically necessary when the testing results in the identification of targeted therapies for patients with advanced cancers, and is not medically necessary when the molecular testing results do not identify targeted therapies for patients.

(1) the molecular panel test is a valuable and cost-effective tool for cancer treatment; (2) the molecular panel is more effective than traditional methods in identifying the appropriate treatment for cancer patients; and (3) the use of the molecular panel can lead to better outcomes and a lower cost of cancer treatment.

(1) the majority of patients who received the expanded molecular panel testing had actionable findings, (2) the majority of actionable findings were not known prior to the testing, and (3) the testing resulted in a change in treatment in 15% of patients.
